long_biography.plain_text:
Koenig grew up in a household where money was tight and worked through the University of Florida before earning an MBA. During college he sold waterbeds from a truck for the shop his older brother had opened. He returned to Fort Lauderdale as a partner with little cash, and the brothers reinvested their earnings while building a fourteen-store chain.

When waterbed demand collapsed, they rebuilt the entire operation around conventional home furnishings, retraining staff and opening the first City Furniture store in 1994. Koenig later broadened the network through an Ashley HomeStore partnership, manufacturing and distribution, while adopting lean-management practices. After his son became chief executive, he remained chairman and a visible supporter of universities, hospitals and youth organisations across South Florida.
